assessment_objectives.objective: the accounts, Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) and access scenarios for which phishing-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is required are defined.
assessment_objectives.scf_defined_parameters: at a minimum, all privileged accounts, all remote access and all access to Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) that store, process or transmit sensitive / regulated data

assessment_objectives.objective: automated mechanisms enforce phishing-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) using authenticators that are cryptographically bound to the verifier's identity (e.g., FIDO2 / WebAuthn or Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)-based authenticators).
authenticator outputs are not accepted by a verifier other than the one to which the authenticator is cryptographically bound, preventing credential relay by an impersonating party.
authenticators that are not phishing-resistant (e.g., SMS, voice, email or push-notification codes) are not accepted as a factor for in-scope accounts and access scenarios.
configurations of in-scope authentication mechanisms are reviewed to confirm phishing-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) remains enforced.
assessment_objectives.scf_defined_parameters: at least quarterly, and upon significant change to the authentication infrastructure
